frontier_answer: Morphological analysis and morphological inflection differ in what they take as input and what they produce as output. Morphological analysis starts with a given word and produces its morphosyntactic description, such as a sequence of morphological tags [E1]. Morphological inflection, by contrast, starts with a lemma plus a set of morphological tags and produces the corresponding inflected word form [E2]. So, analysis is essentially word-form-to-tags, while inflection is lemma-plus-tags-to-word-form [E1][E2].
